target_customer: Developers and small companies hosting web applications that need elastic capacity
problem: Virtual machines and PaaS offerings needed restarts or manual scaling; GoScale resized memory, disk and CPU of Linux containers on the fly.
business_model: Usage-priced cloud hosting (IaaS and PaaS), pricing not found

founders.name: Colin Hayhurst
prior_employers: Century Dynamics (CTO then CEO, acquired by ANSYS)

founders.name: James Cunningham
founders.background_notes: No background published on the YC page.

exit.reason: Not public; the founder discussed the shutdown in a 2020 podcast whose description does not state a cause

competitors.name: Jelastic
competitors.what: PaaS with automatic vertical and horizontal scaling, Java at launch

competitors.name: PHP Fog
competitors.what: Early PHP PaaS with manual scaling

competitors.name: Clever Cloud
competitors.what: PaaS with automatic scalability and pay as you go, launched October 2012
competitors.funding_then: seed from Kima Ventures announced with launch

technical_complexity.rationale: Built an API on Linux Containers and modified system behavior so containers resize live like paravirtualized machines, which commenters on the 2012 launch thread questioned as not new.

defensibility.rationale: Container resizing existed on Solaris, OpenVZ and LXC per launch commenters, and larger clouds could add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented in sources; a low-quality aggregator claims AWS and Google competition, which is unverified.

market_need_then: PHP developers lacked a good elastic host; blog posts in 2012 called it the year of PHP cloud hosting and criticized available PaaS options.

branding.domain_note: Used goscale.com; the site now hosts a historical profile of the company.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical and direct; Show HN title was 'Cloud Scaling in Milliseconds'

branding.brand_signature: iPG, a simulated Paul Graham interview built during the YC application (per the historical site profile)

rebrands.why: Founders said the change of company resulted from their funding sources (Hacker News comment)

branding.community_and_virality: Show HN launch on 2012-08-24 reached 118 points and 60 comments

brand_strength.rationale: Launch post got moderate attention, but no press on the brand itself and a short life.

pivots.why: Founders said the change of company resulted from their funding sources

outcome_analysis: GoScale was a two person London team in YC Summer 2012 offering instantly resizable containers, and the company stopped operating around 2014 per its own historical page. The cause of the shutdown is not public: the founder discussed it in a 2020 podcast, but the episode description gives no reasons and no funding details are available. Competition from established PaaS and cloud vendors is plausible but unsourced, so failure factors are left empty.
notes: Shutdown year 2014 comes from the company's historical site page; loot-drop.io says 2015 with $2.5M burned, an auto-generated page treated as unreliable and not used. Aggregator batch conflict (S12 vs Summer 2012) is the same batch. Competitor entries with 2012 dates only; GoScale itself not found in contemporaneous press apart from the Show HN thread. Cause of failure not public.
